newsitem.title: UK: Next underlying profits up 27 percent.
newsitem.headline: Next underlying profits up 27 percent.

text.p: British fashion retailer Next Plc on Wednesday said first half profits rose nearly 27 percent as sales boomed at both its Next stores and mail order business.
The group, which recently rejoined Britain's FTSE index of 100 top companies, made pretax profits in the first half of 56 million pounds ($87.11 million), up from 50.1 million.
Excluding a six million pound exceptional gain from a disposal last year profits were up by 26.9 percent from 44.1 million pounds.
Sales rose to 406.4 million pounds from 333.3 million. The dividend was increased by 33 percent to 5.0 pence from 3.75 pence.
The results were at the top of market expectations, but Next's shares fell because of disappointment with the retailer's sales so far in the second half. The shares lost 8.5 pence to 591.5 pence.

The company said sales in its stores were 14 percent higher than the previous year in the five weeks from August 12. This included five percent more selling space than the previous year. Mail order sales were 20 percent higher in the same period.
Retail analysts said the increase in sales in the second half was slower than expected. ($1=.6428 Pound)
